Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#linked-properties">https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#linked-properties</a>

entry.title: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport send groups and send-stream prioritization
entry.summary: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport send groups and send-stream prioritization
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+send+groups+and+send%5C-stream+prioritization%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport send groups and send-stream prioritization</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261028" rel="nofollow">Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:34:38 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="8dfbeffff4e5e4a3a3a3cde0e4eeffe2fee2ebf9a3eee2e0">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#6-sending-video-one-stream-per-frame-or-segment-with-send-order">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#6-sending-video-one-stream-per-frame-or-segment-with-send-order</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#7-sending-real-time-game-data-per-stream-with-send-order">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#7-sending-real-time-game-data-per-stream-with-send-order</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#8-managing-bandwidth-with-send-groups">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#8-managing-bandwidth-with-send-groups</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#webtransportsendstream">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#webtransportsendstream</a>
Summary WebTransport already lets sites send data through WritableStreams. This feature lets applications assign outgoing streams to send groups and use sendOrder to prioritize streams within each group. It also provides sending statistics for streams and groups while preserving WritableStream transfer behavior.
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation Real-time applications often send multiple independent flows over one WebTransport session. When those flows compete for bandwidth, applications need to keep one flow from dominating while deciding which streams within each flow should go first. They also need visibility into sending progress so they can understand how those flows are performing.
Initial public proposal No information provided
TAG review No information provided
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Firefox and Safari already expose WebTransportSendStream and the WebTransportSendGroup API; send groups shipped in Firefox 155 and Safari 26.4. Changing Chrome's outgoing streams from plain WritableStream objects to WebTransportSendStream objects therefore aligns their JavaScript type with those browsers. Existing writing behavior and instanceof WritableStream checks remain compatible. Enabling this feature changes outgoing unidirectional streams and the writable side of bidirectional streams from plain WritableStream objects to WebTransportSendStream objects, so exact constructor or prototype check may need updating.
Gecko: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007165">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007165</a>) Firefox exposes WebTransportSendStream as a WritableStream subclass for outgoing WebTransport streams, including streams created by createUnidirectionalStream(). It added WebTransportSendGroup and createSendGroup() in Firefox 155, released September 1, 2026; group assignments are passed to its network implementation - <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/155.0/releasenotes/">https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/155.0/releasenotes/</a> Firefox does not yet provide equivalent statistics behavior. In its current source, WebTransportSendStream.getStats() rejects with NotSupportedError.
WebKit: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/WebTransportSendGroup.json#L52">https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/WebTransportSendGroup.json#L52</a>) WebKit implements WebTransportSendGroup, WebTransportSendStream, sendGroup/sendOrder, both statistics methods, transferability, and the specialized writer. Safari 26.4 includes these WebTransport additions.
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 positive reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Send groups divide outgoing streams into separate bandwidth-sharing groups; sendOrder prioritizes streams within a group, groups are scheduled separately. Developers could mistake a higher sendOrder for a guarantee of delivery order or throughput. Priority is sender-side scheduling, and flow control and network conditions still affect delivery. Stream and group getStats() return asynchronous snapshots; bytesWritten, bytesSent, and bytesAcknowledged represent different stages of transmission, not interchangeable totals. Outgoing streams remain WritableStream subclasses, so existing writing APIs continue to work. The specialized WebTransportWriter is not part of this launch: getWriter() still returns a WritableStreamDefaultWriter.
Activation Enabling the feature changes the runtime type and prototype of outgoing unidirectional streams and the writable side of bidirectional streams from plain WritableStream to WebTransportSendStream for all sites using those streams; sites do not need to call createSendGroup() to observe that change. Code that checks the exact constructor or prototype may behave differently if code assumes exact stream type: stream.constructor === WritableStream or Object.getPrototypeOf(stream) === WritableStream.prototype. Existing stream writes should continue to work, and no server change is needed to use the new client-side priority controls. Transfer of existing send streams must continue working before activation.
Security No new network capability or origin boundary is introduced. The API operates only on streams belonging to an existing secure-context WebTransport session. A send group from another WebTransport object is rejected. Statistics expose byte counters for the application's own streams and groups.
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. This is an additive API on existing WebTransport streams and does not change connection establishment or network behavior.
Debuggability The stream's sendGroup and sendOrder values are directly observable from script. Both stream and group getStats() expose bytesWritten, bytesSent, and bytesAcknowledged; group statistics aggregate streams in that group. DevTools does not currently provide dedicated WebTransport stream inspection, so developers primarily diagnose this API through script and application logging.
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendgroup.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendgroup.https.any.html</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendorder.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendorder.https.any.html</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendstream-bad-chunk.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/sendstream-bad-chunk.https.any.html</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/send-stream-stats.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/send-stream-stats.https.any.html</a>
Flag name on about://flags enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportSendGroup
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://crbug.com/568825278">https://crbug.com/568825278</a>
Availability expectation Firefox 155 ships createSendGroup(), and Safari 26.4 ships WebTransport with the corresponding WebKit group and send-stream interfaces. Chrome shipping would make the API shape available across the major engines.
Adoption expectation Adoption is expected mainly among existing WebTransport applications with multiple concurrent streams and latency-sensitive traffic.
Adoption plan Adoption is expected to occur organically through WebTransport documentation, examples, and client library support. Developers can progressively enhance existing code by feature-detecting getStats().
Non-OSS dependencies
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function? No
Estimated milestones
Shipping on desktop 159
DevTrial on desktop 153
Shipping on Android 159
DevTrial on Android 153
Shipping on WebView 159
Anticipated spec changes
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). None known for the WebTransportSendStream or WebTransportSendGroup.

To view this discussion visit <a rel="nofollow" href="https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/d/msgid/blink-dev/6ae2867d.4000571a.28172.010c.GAE%40google.com">https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/d/msgid/blink-dev/6ae2867d.4000571a.28172.010c.GAE%40google.com</a>. </pre>

<a rel="nofollow" href="https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uCVUqYGKgsCCu7LEtEdO3Yuea-MT-I2XsU6Eoe3mlQI/edit?usp=sharing">https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uCVUqYGKgsCCu7LEtEdO3Yuea-MT-I2XsU6Eoe3mlQI/edit?usp=sharing</a>
Summary Adds structured JavaScript access to SVG path data through three methods on SVGPathElement: getPathData() reads the path as an array of {type, values} objects containing each segment's command and numeric parameters. setPathData() updates the path from such an array, getPathSegmentAtLength() returns the segment at a specified distance along the path. These methods let developers inspect, edit, and construct paths without manually parsing or serializing the d attribute. The optional getPathData({normalize: true}) setting simplifies path data to absolute move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands (M, L, C, and Z). All three APIs operate on the base value of the d attribute, not CSS-computed or animated values.
Blink component Blink>SVG
Web Feature ID No information provided
Motivation In Chromium, inspecting or modifying individual SVG path segments requires parsing and serializing the d attribute string, often using third-party libraries. This makes tasks such as path animation, hit-testing, and programmatic path construction unnecessarily complex and error-prone. The previous SVGPathSegList API was removed in Chromium 48 because of its complex live mutation model, numerous factory methods, and underspecified edge cases. Developers have since relied on polyfills to restore structured access. Implementing the SVG Working Group's replacement API provides a simpler, standardized way to read and modify path segments without custom string parsing or polyfills.
Initial public proposal No information provided

Other signals:

Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? None. The feature adds new methods to SVGPathElement that developers can feature-detect before use.

Summary It was resolved in the CSSWG that we should introduce the flow-start/end keywords as value aliases for the existing flex-start/end keywords. These are needed for alignment in the case of placement reversals.
flow-start in CSS Grid-Lanes would indicate the starting edge of the container at which placement begins, which is useful in the case where placement is reversed (`fill-reverse`, `track-reverse`, discussed in this CSSWG issue: [css-grid-3][masonry] item-flow row vs. column in masonry layouts · Issue #12803 · w3c/csswg-drafts). Because these are acting as value aliases, we expect flex-start/end to follow the logical directions in Grid Lanes, as well, which will expand the definition of these keywords from only applying special behavior in flexbox to applying to any layout mode whose logical start/end is different from its physical start/end.
For serialization, if either flex-start/end or flow-start/end is used, the returned serialized value should be flow-start/end.

entry.summary: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport keying material export
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+keying+material+export%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport keying material export</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261021" rel="nofollow">Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:09:31 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="6a18034444442a0902180507031f074405180d">[email protected]</a>, <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="c4a9abaaada7eaeaea84a9ada7b6abb7aba2b0eaa7aba9">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-exportkeyingmaterial">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-exportkeyingmaterial</a>
Summary Adds WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial(), which allows an application to derive cryptographic keying material bound to an established WebTransport session. The method accepts application provided binary label and context values and a requested output length and returns a Promise<Uint8Array>. Chromium supports label and context values up to 255 bytes and output lengths from 1 through 4096 bytes. For WebTransport over HTTP/3, Chromium includes the WebTransport CONNECT stream ID in the TLS exporter context. This ensures that separate WebTransport sessions derive different keying material even when they share the same underlying HTTP/3 connection.
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation Applications sometimes need cryptographic keying material bound to an authenticated transport session, for example to bind an application protocol, authentication exchange, or application-level encryption context to a WebTransport session without performing an additional key exchange. TLS exporters derive application-specific secret material without exposing the TLS traffic keys. WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial() exposes this mechanism through application-provided binary label and context values and an explicit output length. Multiple WebTransport sessions can share one HTTP/3 connection. Chromium therefore includes the WebTransport CONNECT stream ID in the exporter context, ensuring that different sessions derive different keying material even when callers use identical application labels and contexts.
Initial public proposal <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/411">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/411</a>
TAG review This is an incremental method within the existing WebTransport specification. WebTransport has an umbrella TAG review, and a separate feature-level review is not currently planned.
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Interoperability risk: Medium. The current WebTransport specification and upstream WPT define the required three-argument exportKeyingMaterial(label, context, outputLength) method. Chromium and WebKit implement this shape. Firefox currently exposes the earlier two-argument form without outputLength , so API-shape interoperability is not yet complete. Implementations and servers must also use the same fixed exporter label and exporter-context construction, including the WebTransport session ID, application label, application context, and requested output length. A mismatch produces different bytes without an explicit protocol error. Compatibility risk: Low. The method is additive and does not change existing WebTransport construction, streams, datagrams, or connection behavior. Applications can use feature detection with "exportKeyingMaterial" in WebTransport.prototype.
Gecko: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079306">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079306</a>) Firefox is updating its implementation to the current three-argument API.
WebKit: In development (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/69982">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/69982</a>) WebKit has landed an implementation of the current three-argument WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial(label, context, outputLength) API.
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/411">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/411</a>) The proposal received 10 👍 reactions and requests from developers, including libp2p, for TLS-session binding and channel-binding use cases.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Ergonomics risk is moderate because this is a low-level cryptographic primitive. Binary BufferSource label and context values avoid string-encoding ambiguity, while the explicit output length avoids an implicit key-size choice. Calls made while the WebTransport session is connecting are queued until the connection is established. Calls after closure or failure reject with InvalidStateError . Label or context values over 255 bytes and zero or unsupported output lengths reject with RangeError . Documentation should recommend protocol-specific domain-separation values and secure handling of the resulting bytes.
Activation Activation risk is moderate but bounded. The API is additive and has no effect unless a site explicitly invokes it. It introduces no new network messages or additional protocol negotiation. The main activation risk is a mismatch between client and server implementations in the exporter construction, including the fixed exporter label, WebTransport session ID serialization, application label or context, and output length. Such a mismatch causes the endpoints to derive different bytes without an explicit error. Chromium mitigates this risk through validation in Blink and across the renderer/network-service boundary, fixed input limits, session-specific domain separation, lifecycle checks, unit and Web Platform Tests, and the WebTransportExportKeyingMaterial runtime/Finch feature gate.
Security This API exposes secret-derived material to script and therefore requires careful domain separation and lifecycle handling. It does not expose TLS traffic keys or allow callers to decrypt WebTransport traffic. Chromium uses the fixed TLS exporter label "EXPORTER-WebTransport" and constructs an exporter context containing the WebTransport CONNECT stream ID, application label, and application context. Including the CONNECT stream ID prevents different WebTransport sessions sharing one HTTP/3 connection from deriving identical keying material when given the same application inputs. Chromium limits label and context values to 255 bytes and output to 4096 bytes, validates requests in both Blink and the network service, verifies the returned output length, and rejects calls after the session has closed or failed. Applications remain responsible for treating the result as secret keying material and using protocol-specific label and context values Security questionnaire: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/security-questionnaire.md">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/security-questionnaire.md</a>
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. This is an additive API implemented in shared Blink and network-service code. The CL updates the Android WebView Web-exposed interface expectation and requires no WebView-specific integration. Stable WebView exposure should follow the existing availability and launch process for WebTransport in WebView.
Debuggability Developers can inspect the label, context, output length, returned Uint8Array, and any rejected exception through JavaScript breakpoints or the Console. CDP exposes WebTransport creation, connection-establishment, and closure events. NetLog provides additional WebTransport version, QUIC lifecycle, and stream diagnostics. Neither CDP nor NetLog records exporter invocations, exported bytes, or compares the client-derived value with the server-derived value. A client/server derivation mismatch therefore requires server cooperation, preferably through a key-confirmation challenge or MAC rather than logging raw keying material.
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes All Blink platforms on which WebTransport over HTTP/3 is supported. The Web-exposed implementation is cross-platform Blink code, while key derivation uses Chromium's existing HTTP/3/QUIC TLS exporter path.
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/export-keying-material.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/export-keying-material.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>,
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
Flag name on about://flags chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportExportKeyingMaterial
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/556304550">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/556304550</a>
Measurement Measure correctness and interoperability through Web Platform Tests, the WebTransport IDL harness, wpt.fyi results, and feedback from WebTransport application and server implementers. Usage will be measured with a WebFeature use counter recorded when WebTransport.exportKeyingMaterial() is called. No dedicated UMA metric is currently planned, the use counter is sufficient to measure web-exposed API adoption
Availability expectation Expected to become available across major browser engines as part of the W3C WebTransport specification. WebKit has landed the current three-argument API in WebKit main, although stable Safari availability has not yet been verified. Firefox currently implements the earlier two-argument form without the required outputLength argument.
Adoption expectation Expected to be used by specialized WebTransport protocols that require transport-bound authentication, channel binding, or application key derivation. It is not expected to be used by most basic WebTransport applications.
Adoption plan Adoption is expected to occur through WebTransport documentation, interoperable WPT coverage, and use by protocol implementations that require transport-bound keying material. No origin trial or broad developer campaign is currently planned
Estimated milestones
Shipping on desktop 158
Shipping on Android 158
Shipping on WebView 158
Anticipated spec changes
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). No API-shape changes are currently anticipated. Chromium implements the current required three-argument method and matches the WebTransport-over-HTTP/3 exporter construction, including the fixed exporter label and session-specific context encoding. <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/791">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/791</a> tracks making the specification's reference to the protocol-level exporter construction more explicit. This is currently an editorial clarity issue rather than a known behavior change.

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+Datagram+readable+stream+type%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport Datagram readable stream type</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261021" rel="nofollow">Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:52:50 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="9be9f2b5b5b5dbf8f3e9f4f6f2eef6b5f4e9fc">[email protected]</a>, <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="f39e9c9d9a90ddddddb39e9a90819c809c9587dd909c9e">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransportoptions-datagramsreadabletype">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransportoptions-datagramsreadabletype</a>
Summary Adds the WebTransportOptions.datagramsReadableType constructor option. By default, incoming WebTransport Datagrams are exposed through a default ReadableStream . Applications that require BYOB reading can request a readable byte stream by setting datagramsReadableType: "bytes" .
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation WebTransport Datagrams are discrete messages rather than an undifferentiated byte sequence. A readable byte stream can lose empty Datagrams and can lose message boundaries when BYOB reads use a minimum byte count spanning multiple Datagrams. Making a default ReadableStream the default preserves Datagram boundaries and empty Datagrams. Applications that benefit from BYOB allocation control can explicitly opt into the byte-stream behavior.
Initial public proposal No information provided
TAG review Not applicable — this is a small incremental addition within the existing WebTransport specification.
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Interoperability risk is low to medium. The API and default-stream behavior are defined in the WebTransport specification and covered by WPT. Firefox already uses a default non-byte stream when the option is omitted, but does not yet support the explicit "bytes" mode in current public test runs. Compatibility risk is mitigated by runtime gating. Chromium historically exposed the Datagram readable as a byte stream, so enabling the feature changes the default behavior: existing applications using a BYOB reader without specifying datagramsReadableType: "bytes" would fail. Applications using ordinary readers continue to receive Uint8Array chunks
Gecko: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007755">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007755</a>) Firefox is implementing datagramsReadableType: "bytes" and BYOB Datagram reads
WebKit: In development (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=319830">https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=319830</a>) WebKit main implements the standardized datagramsReadableType option
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 👍 reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Low. The default stream better matches Datagram message semantics. Applications needing BYOB allocation control must explicitly opt into "bytes" , making the semantic tradeoff visible in application code.
Activation The main activation risk is existing Chromium-specific code assuming that transport.datagrams.readable always supports BYOB readers. Such applications must explicitly request datagramsReadableType: "bytes" . The feature remains experimentally gated while compatibility and interoperability are evaluated.
Security Low. The option changes only the JavaScript stream adapter used to expose already-received Datagrams. It does not provide additional network access, expose new information, or alter WebTransport's secure-context and connection security requirements.
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. The implementation is cross-platform Blink code and requires no WebView-specific integration. The primary compatibility consideration is the same as Chrome: applications using a BYOB reader must explicitly request datagramsReadableType: "bytes" .
Debuggability No feature-specific DevTools UI is required. Applications can inspect whether datagrams.readable supports BYOB by attempting to acquire a BYOB reader. Existing WebTransport logging, NetLog, and DevTools network diagnostics remain available for connection and Datagram issues.
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes Yes. Implemented in cross-platform Blink code without platform-specific dependencies.
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/datagrams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/datagrams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
Flag name on about://flags chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportDatagramsReadableType
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/547572475">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/547572475</a>
Availability expectation WebKit has implemented the option and corresponding default-stream behavior in its main branch. Firefox implements the default non-byte stream behavior, although explicit "bytes" /BYOB mode does not yet pass current public WPT runs. Broad availability is expected as implementations converge on the WebTransport specification.
Adoption expectation Adoption is expected mainly among WebTransport applications that use BYOB readers or need reliable preservation of Datagram message boundaries. Most applications using ordinary readers require no code changes.
Adoption plan Adoption is expected through WebTransport documentation and Interop 2026 visibility. Existing Chromium applications using BYOB readers will need to explicitly set datagramsReadableType: "bytes" when the feature is enabled.
Estimated milestones

DevTrial on desktop 155
Shipping on Android 159
DevTrial on Android 155
Shipping on WebView 159
Anticipated spec changes

Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). <div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Re%5C%3A+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+Fetch+API%5C%3A+Forward+reason+from+AbortController+to+fetch+Response%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Ship: Fetch API: Forward reason from AbortController to fetch Response</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22%27Daniel+Clark%27+via+blink%5C-dev%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">'Daniel Clark' via blink-dev</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260819" rel="nofollow">Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:50:51 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>To be clear on what I mean below is that you should enable the feature in Canary so that it goes through canary/dev/beta first before reaching stable. So if done now that’d ship to Stable in 154.</pre><pre>
If that still doesn’t leave 4 weeks lead time you can leave that "Announcement lead time” box unchecked if it hasn’t been unchanged for that long and still request the Adoption review (after ensuring the other boxes are completed if they apply). The owners of that gate can comment if they think it needs more lead time; IMO it will likely be fine.
From: Taylor Brandstetter <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="5a3e3f3b3e387474741a3d35353d363f74393537">[email protected]</a>> Date: Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 12:37 PM To: Daniel Clark <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="e88c8986c6c6c6a885818b9a879b878e9cc68b8785">[email protected]</a>> Cc: blink-dev <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="56343a3f383d7b32332016353e24393b3f233b78392431">[email protected]</a>>; <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="2a5946434d420404046a4942584547435f470445584d">[email protected]</a> <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="99eaf5f0fef1edf5e0b7b7b7d9faf1ebf6f4f0ecf4b7f6ebfe">[email protected]</a>>; Chromestatus <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="5130357f7f7f1132237c2225302524227f30212122213e253c30383d7f323e3c">[email protected]</a>>; Adam Rice <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="03716a2d2d2d43646c6c646f662d606c6e">[email protected]</a>> Subject: Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Ship: Fetch API: Forward reason from AbortController to fetch Response
You don't often get email from <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="a8cccdc9ccca868686e8cfc7c7cfc4cd86cbc7c5">[email protected]</a>. Learn why this is important<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://aka.ms/LearnAboutSenderIdentification">https://aka.ms/LearnAboutSenderIdentification</a>> The Adoption gate should be filled out before shipping...where did you see a reference to "stable for four weeks"?
One of the checkboxes is "Announcement lead time. This feature's name, summary, and milestones have been unchanged for the past four weeks".
Which I assumed didn't apply since I changed the milestone (153->154). However, if we ship it by enabling the feature flag on stable immediately—rather than going through canary/dev/beta first—it could actually ship in 153, as the code is ready. Shall I revert that change and proceed with the Adoption prepare to ship? The feature entry hasn't even existed for four weeks, though, is that a problem?
On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 8:12 AM 'Dan Clark' via blink-dev <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="8defe1e4e3e6a0e9e8fbcdeee5ffe2e0e4f8e0a3e2ffea">[email protected]</a><<a rel="nofollow" href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#7416181d1a1f5910110234171c061b191d01195a1b0613">mailto:<span class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="e587898c8b8ec8818093a5868d978a888c9088cb8a9782">[email protected]</span></a>>> wrote: LGTM2, thanks for helping us consider the compat risks here. My recommendation to ship "normally" is to just set the feature flag to "stable" in main and let the change roll out through the normal release channels. Keep an eye out for bugs, and if there is some problem, that's when you'd use Finch to set the flag back off in the stable channel. As a non-Googler I can't speak to the process details of that, but hopefully a Googler can help if that does become needed.
On Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 2:26:34 PM UTC-7 Taylor Brandstetter wrote: > We shouldn’t [ship normally] without trying to understand the risk, though. > What do you expect potential compatibility issues to look like for this? Do > developers often have logic branching on specific abort values for these > promises versus just logging them? Do we have Use Counters that could put a > high bar on the risk, like a counter for how often already-completed fetches > are aborted with a reason, or how often the Response methods are called for a > fetch in this state?
I don't see any use counters specifically for providing an abort reason, no. Branching logic on the error from the promises would be the risk, although there's a good chance that we were just being overly cautious. I have no reason to believe this would be particularly common. If others are ok with it, I would suggest just shipping normally with 154. You mentioned being ready to roll back via finch; does that mean we would keep the change gated behind a flag, but roll it out to 100% immediately for 154 when it branches? I'm not very familiar with finch (or this process) so bear with me.
I requested the WebKit signal (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/711">https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/711</a>) and the other Prepare to Ship reviews, which I assume should be fairly trivial. I haven't requested Prepare to Ship for Adoption yet as it requires the feature to be stable for four weeks, and I just changed the milestone to 154.
On Monday, August 17, 2026 at 11:44:29 AM UTC-7 Alex Russell wrote: Hey Taylor,
I'm going to LGTM1 this on the basis that we do not have compatible behaviour between WebKit/Chromium and Gecko at the moment, reducing the likely risk of breakage. That said, we do need the other review bits filled in (via chromestatus), and my LGTM is contingent on those, as well as requests for positions to Mozilla and WebKit.
Best,
Alex
On Monday, August 17, 2026 at 8:45:19 AM UTC-7 Taylor Brandstetter wrote: > Can you please give a more specific link into the part of the spec that > defines this behavior?
Sure thing; the body methods point to the steps for consuming a body: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-body-consume-body">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-body-consume-body</a>
Which point to the steps for fully reading a body: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#body-fully-read">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#body-fully-read</a>
Which say to read all the bytes from the reader.
And regarding the reader, the main abort steps (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-network-fetch">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-network-fetch</a>) say:
1. If fetchParams is aborted<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-aborted">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-aborted</a>>, then:
* Set response’s aborted flag<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-aborted">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-aborted</a>>.
* If stream is readable<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestream-readable">https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestream-readable</a>>, then error<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestream-error">https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#readablestream-error</a>> stream with the result of deserialize a serialized abort reason<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#deserialize-a-serialized-abort-reason">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#deserialize-a-serialized-abort-reason</a>> given fetchParams’s controller<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-controller">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-params-controller</a>>’s serialized abort reason<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-serialized-abort-reason">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller-serialized-abort-reason</a>> and an implementation-defined<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined">https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined</a>> realm<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://tc39.es/ecma262/#realm">https://tc39.es/ecma262/#realm</a>>.
So, both the readable stream and all the body methods consuming it should be errored with the abort reason.
> Can you request a WebKit signal?
I didn't realize it was necessary just for filling a gap in the implementation, but the wide review documentation<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.chromium.org/blink/launching-features/wide-review/">https://www.chromium.org/blink/launching-features/wide-review/</a>> does call this case out, so I will request a signal and update the feature later.
> I'm still unclear on which tests cover this change.
I called them out there; "response.X() rejects with abort reason if already aborted" (for each body method) and "Stream errors once aborted with abort reason". They fail on everything but Firefox (well except for the latter which doesn't run on Firefox); I'm assuming the dashboard wasn't updated when you responded but you can see the failures now. > Can you say more about this roll out plan? This doesn't seem like the kind of > thing that would need to be rolled out gradually via experiment.
@ricea had suggested using an experiment, I assume because the use of fetch is so widespread and changing the type of error that's thrown could have consequences, even if it's the intended behavior. But I'll let him comment on that himself if he has anything to add. > Lastly please request the other "Prepare to Ship" reviews in the chromestatus > entry (Privacy, WP Security, etc).
Will do. Thanks for your review, Dan. On Monday, August 10, 2026 at 12:11:55 PM UTC-7 Dan Clark wrote: > Specification > <a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org</a><<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/</a>>
Can you please give a more specific link into the part of the spec that defines this behavior?
> WebKit: No signal
Can you request a WebKit signal?
> Is this feature fully tested by > web-platform-tests<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>? > Yes > <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/api/abort/general.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/api/abort/general.any.html</a> Specifically the > tests: * response.arrayBuffer() rejects with abort reason if already aborted > (and other response methods such as body()) * Stream errors once aborted with > abort reason. Underlying connection closed.
I'm still unclear on which tests cover this change. Looking at the test results<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/api/abort/general.any.html?label=master&product=chrome%5Bstable%5D&product=edge%5Bexperimental%5D&product=firefox%5Bexperimental%5D&product=safari%5Bexperimental%5D&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/api/abort/general.any.html?label=master&product=chrome%5Bstable%5D&product=edge%5Bexperimental%5D&product=firefox%5Bexperimental%5D&product=safari%5Bexperimental%5D&aligned</a>> all are already passing in Chrome Stable except for "Readable stream synchronously cancels with AbortError if aborted before reading" which doesn't seem to match this scenario.
> Rollout plan > (RARE) Experiment users ramp up over time
Can you say more about this roll out plan? This doesn't seem like the kind of thing that would need to be rolled out gradually via experiment.
Lastly please request the other "Prepare to Ship" reviews in the chromestatus entry (Privacy, WP Security, etc).
Thanks, Dan

Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org</a><<a rel="nofollow" href="https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/">https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/</a>>
Summary An AbortController can be passed into fetch to allow a request to be aborted; this is already supported see <a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5631483679080448">https://chromestatus.com/feature/5631483679080448</a> When calling abort, you can optionally pass in an "abort reason", and the original fetch promise if it hasn't resolved should be rejected with that reason. This is already working as intended. *However*, if the fetch promise *has* resolved (after reading the header), but the body has not yet been fully read, this is also intended to propagate the abort reason to the Response methods such as Response.blob(), as well as the ReadableStream Response.body. This part is not currently working; the relevant Promises instead are rejected with generic AbortErrors. Firefox at least is compliant here but chromium/Edge/Safari are not.

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+Pause+media+playback+on+not%5C-visible+iframes%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: Pause media playback on not-visible iframes</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260904" rel="nofollow">Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:49:31 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="e3848281918a868f8191cdcdcda38e8a80918c908c8597cd808c8e">[email protected]</a>, <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="73000716055d5d5d331e1a10011c001c15075d101c1e">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md">https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wicg.github.io/iframe-media-pausing">https://wicg.github.io/iframe-media-pausing</a>
Summary Adds a "media-playback-while-not-visible" permission policy to allow embedders to pause audible media playback of embedded iframes which are currently hidden - ie "display" property set to "none"; "visibility" property set to "hidden"; or zero-area (width or height equal to 0). While hidden, attempts made by the embedded iframe to render audible media will be blocked. When the frame is shown again the prohibitions should be lifted. This should allow developers to build more user-friendly experiences and to also improve the performance by letting the browser handle the playback of content that is not visible to users.
Blink component Blink>Media
Web Feature ID <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4292">https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4292</a>
Motivation Web applications that host embedded media content via iframes may wish to respond to application input by temporarily hiding the media content. These applications may not want to unload the entire iframe when it's not rendered since it could generate user-perceptible performance and experience issues when showing the media content again. At the same time, the user could have a negative experience if the media continues to play and emit audio when not rendered. This proposal aims to provide web applications with the ability to control embedded media content in such a way that guarantees their users have a good experience when the iframe's render status is changed.
Initial public proposal No information provided
TAG review <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1084">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1084</a>
TAG review status Issues addressed
Origin Trial Name media-playback-while-not-visible Permission Policy
Goals for experimentation Gather feedback from web developers and validate that the current prototype implementation works as expected. We have added telemetry to measure how the feature is being exercised by users: - HTMLMediaElement's: - # of pauses while hidden - # of pauses because got hidden during playback - WebAudio AudioContext's - # of interruptions while hidden - # of interruptions because got hidden during playback
Chromium Trial Name MediaPlaybackWhileNotVisiblePermissionPolicy

Safari also seems to be unofficially supportive: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208#issuecomment-3060151372">https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208#issuecomment-3060151372</a>

A commenter mentioned that the proposal fits well within the Permissions Policy API specification. They also agree that there is no workaround for this problem using current web API's. Feedback has been addressed to also include other invisibility scenarios like zero-area (height or width equal to 0) and to change the API name from "not-rendered" to "not-visible".
Other signals:
Ergonomics This feature will be used with other audio rendering API's, like HTMLMediaElement and Web Audio. This new behavior should only take effect if web pages explicitly opt-in by overriding the permission policy's default state. Moreover, once the permission policy is used, it should help Chromium to be more optimized by pausing audio rendering for content that is not visible for the user.

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+CSS+position%5C-visibility%5C%3Aanchor%5C%7Bs%5C%7D%5C-valid%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: CSS position-visibility:anchor{s}-valid</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22%27Mason+Freed%27+via+blink%5C-dev%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">'Mason Freed' via blink-dev</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260929" rel="nofollow">Tue, 29 Sep 2026 07:48:03 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre> On Monday, September 28, 2026 at 11:32:35 AM UTC-7 Dan Clark wrote:

<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility">https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility</a>>*
The only of these tests I saw covering anchor-valid is this one: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-visibility-anchor-valid.tentative.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-visibility-anchor-valid.tentative.html</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="http://Is%20this%20feature%20fully%20tested%20by%20web-platform-tests?%20Yes%20https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility">http://Is%20this%20feature%20fully%20tested%20by%20web-platform-tests?%20Yes%20https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility</a>> .
Maybe not too many tests are needed, but does this fully cover the behavior called out in the summary? "[The new version is] better defined to be clear that only the default anchor matters , resolving a lot of ambiguity"?
Sorry, I should have added to that response that my CL to implement the feature <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://crrev.com/c/8453827">https://crrev.com/c/8453827</a>> adds more testing.
E.g. the test shows that this is hidden: <div id="target2" class="target" style="top: anchor(--does-not-exist bottom);">target2</div>
But it'd be nice to include a case where position-anchor is unset but anchor() refers to an anchor name that actually does exist: <div id="target3" class="target" style="top: anchor(--a1 bottom);">target2</div>
I believe this is "Case 7" from the new position-visibility-anchor-valid-001.html test.
And maybe a similar set of checks with anchor-size().
This is indeed missing. I'll land another CL to add test cases for anchor-size like this - thanks for the suggestion.
Another case that seems important to have is an element that has a valid default anchor, but another anchor it depends on doesn't resolve. If I'm understanding correctly that would have resulted in the element being hidden in the original proposal <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7758#issuecomment-1965540529">https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7758#issuecomment-1965540529</a>>, but in the current proposal the element would be shown, since only the default anchor matters.
Also a good (missing) suggestion. I'll add it!
Thanks, Mason

entry.summary: Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Deprecate and Remove: Topics API
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Re%5C%3A+Intent+to+Deprecate+and+Remove%5C%3A+Topics+API%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Deprecate and Remove: Topics API</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Mike+Taylor%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Mike Taylor</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260930" rel="nofollow">Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:22:25 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2
On 9/30/26 8:29 a.m., Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM1</pre><pre>
On Thu, Sep 24, 2026 at 8:19 AM Yao Xiao <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="95ecf4fabbbbbbd5f6fde7faf8fce0f8bbfae7f2">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
Hi API Owners,
We have reached 1% on Stable (M153+) with no regressions or known breakage. The current usage is at 2% <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>. We would like to request approval to proceed with the staged deprecation rollout:
* 10% Stable: Hold for 2 weeks (through Oct 15) * 100% Stable: Target launch after Oct 15
Thanks for your consideration.
Best regards, Yao
On Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 11:14:19 AM UTC-4 Alex Russell wrote:
LGTM3 on the condition that the rollout of this change is done progressively via Finch so we can monitor for breakage and roll back if things go sideways. Thanks for taking care not to break the web.
Best,
Alex
On Thursday, June 25, 2026 at 10:04:36 AM UTC-7 Chris Harrelson wrote:
LGTM2. Sorry for the delay.
On Thu, Jun 25, 2026 at 9:57 AM Yoav Weiss (@Shopify) <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="85fceae4f3f2e0abababc5e6edf7eae8ecf0e8abeaf7e2">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
LGTM1
On Fri, Jun 12, 2026 at 1:18 AM Yao Xiao <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="bdc4dcd2939393fdded5cfd2d0d4c8d093d2cfda">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
Hi API Owners, The Topics API was deprecated in Chrome-144 with a plan to remove it in Chrome-150. Currently the usage is 4.9% of page
loads.<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>We are proposing the following as next steps for removal and associated timelines: 1. M150: Remove all Ads API-related entries from Chrome settings and UI surfaces (e.g., chrome://settings/adPrivacy) via field trial. After this point, all API invocations for field-trial enabled browsers will always reject. Since the API can already be disabled for one of many reasons, scripts must already handle such rejections (or they’re already significantly broken).2. M152: Permanently remove the underlying implementation code for the API, and replace it with a lightweight stub API. The stub will remain removable via field trial.
3. M152 Canary/Beta: Begin a controlled rollout of the stub API removal via a field trial.4. M152 Stable: Assuming there are no regressions or breakage after reaching 1% stable, we will request additional approval for full removal at this stage.
At this time, we are seeking LGTMs for steps #2 and #3.
Thanks,
Yao
On Wednesday, November 12, 2025 at 11:36:22 AM UTC-5 Daniel Bratell wrote:
LGTM3 according to Vlad's plan.
/Daniel
On 2025-11-12 17:19, Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2 with the same conditions Vlad mentioned.
On Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 8:16 AM Vladimir Levin <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="aadcc7da848484eac9c2d8c5c7c3dfc784c5d8cd">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
LGTM1 to deprecate. The plan to keep deprecation for 6 milestones also sounds good. Please come back after to this thread at a time when you think the removal can proceed. Since the amount of page loads is extremely high, we would like to reserve the right to pause the removal if this amount of page loads does not decrease substantially.
On Friday, November 7, 2025 at 1:12:36 PM UTC-5 Yao Xiao wrote:
Intent to Deprecate and Remove: Topics API
Contact emails
<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="740d151b5a5a5a34171c061b191d01195a1b0613">[email protected]</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#08716967262626486b607a6765617d6526677a6f">mailto:<span class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="2c554d430202026c4f445e434145594102435e4b">[email protected]</span></a>>
Explainer
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics">https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics">https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics</a>>
Specification
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/">https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/">https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/</a>>
Summary
The Topics API is a privacy-preserving web API to enable ad-targeting based on a person’s general browsing interests, without exposing their exact browsing history.
Following Chrome's announcement that the current approach to third-party cookies will be maintained, we are now planning to deprecate and remove the Topics API (along with other Privacy Sandbox APIs).
The following API surfaces will be affected:
*
The JavaScript function `document.browsingTopics()` will be removed.
*
The `browsingtopics` attribute on <iframe> and <img> elements will be ignored.
*
The `browsingTopics` option in the fetch() API's RequestInit will be a no-op.
*
Consequently, the `Sec-Browsing-Topics` request header will no longer be sent, and the `Observe-Browsing-Topics` response header will no longer be honored.
*
The "browsing-topics" and "interest-cohort" permissions policy features will be removed.
Blink component
Blink>TopicsAPI
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ETopicsAPI%22">https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ETopicsAPI%22</a>>
Web Feature ID
None
Motivation
Chrome has announced that the current approach to third-party cookies will be maintained. Given this, we expect adoption to decrease over time (currently at 13%
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>of page loads) as interest based advertising will remain possible in Chrome using third-party cookies. Further, other browser engines have not signaled interest in launching the API. See also the initial public proposal below.
Initial public proposal
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/">https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/">https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/</a>>.
Possible breakage
Sites that rely on Topics API for targeting will experience utility impact.
If usage warrants, we will take steps to avoid any risk of page breakage, e.g. by temporarily retaining a stub implementation of `document.browsingTopics()` that mimics current behavior when a user has no topics to return. However, since Topics is not enabled by default for all users, sites should already be using feature detection, which makes the risks of breakage low.
Debuggability
N/A
Requires code in //chrome?
True
Estimated milestones
Deprecate in M144 and then remove in M150.
Currently, ~13%
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>of page loads use Topics API. These are driven by a small number of third-party ad tech scripts present on a large number of sites. We will continue to monitor usage as well as provide comprehensive updates on privacysandbox.google.com <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://goo.gle/ps-status">http://goo.gle/ps-status</a>>with the status of the API and deprecation plans.
We will also proactively work toward reducing usage to a low level once the intent is approved, including disallowing any new enrollment sign-ups, and contacting all enrolled sites that use the Privacy Sandbox APIs to inform them about the deprecation timelines.

entry.title: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes
entry.summary: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+reliability+attributes%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261007" rel="nofollow">Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:23:32 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="0d7f642323234d6e657f626064786023627f6a">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#transport-modes">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#transport-modes</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-reliability">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-reliability</a>
Summary Adds the WebTransport.reliability instance attribute and static WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly attribute. These APIs indicate whether the user agent supports WebTransport over exclusively reliable connections and whether an established session supports unreliable transport such as datagrams. In Chromium, reliability initially returns "pending" and changes to "supports-unreliable" after an HTTP/3 WebTransport connection is established. Since Chromium does not currently support HTTP/2 fallback, WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly returns false; any successfully established session uses HTTP/3 and supports unreliable datagrams.
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation WebTransport may operate over connections with different reliability capabilities. Applications such as games, interactive media, and real-time collaboration tools need to know whether unreliable datagrams are available before selecting their transport strategy. WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly reports whether the user agent supports WebTransport over exclusively reliable connections. The per-session reliability attribute is "pending" while connecting and becomes "reliable-only" or "supports-unreliable" once the transport is known. Chromium currently implements WebTransport over HTTP/3 with unreliable datagram support, so established sessions report "supports-unreliable" and supportsReliableOnly returns false.
Initial public proposal <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/385">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/385</a>
TAG review This is a small incremental implementation of attributes already defined in the existing W3C WebTransport specification. It does not introduce a new API design or Chromium-specific extension
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Compatibility risk is low because both attributes are additive and do not change existing WebTransport behavior. Interoperability risk is low because the attributes and their "pending" , "reliable-only" , and "supports-unreliable" values are defined by the W3C WebTransport specification. Equivalent APIs are implemented or partially implemented in WebKit and Firefox, and WebTransport is an Interop 2026 focus area.
Gecko: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1709355">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1709355</a>)
WebKit: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/55124">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/55124</a>)
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 👍 reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Ergonomics risk is low. reliability synchronously returns "pending" while connecting, and applications can await WebTransport.ready before reading its final value. The static supportsReliableOnly attribute enables capability detection before creating a connection.
Activation Activation risk is low. This is an additive API that does not change existing WebTransport behavior or require server changes. Developers can use standard feature detection and retain existing fallbacks for older browsers.
Security No new network capability or sensitive information is exposed. The attributes report whether an implementation or session supports exclusively reliable or unreliable WebTransport, which is already observable through the available WebTransport APIs. They expose no server data, credentials, addresses, or user-specific information.
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. This is an additive API surface and does not modify the behavior of existing WebTransport connections. WebView applications that do not use the attributes are unaffected
Debuggability The attributes can be inspected directly from JavaScript or the Chrome DevTools Console. Developers can inspect transport.reliability before and after transport.ready resolves and inspect WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly without creating a connection. No additional DevTools-specific support is required
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes All Blink platforms on which WebTransport is supported. The implementation is in cross-platform Blink code.
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes WPT coverage verifies that: • Initial "pending" state. • Transition after ready . • Web IDL exposure. Static attribute and initial state: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a> State after connection establishment: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a> IDL harness: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
Flag name on about://flags chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportReliability
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/545636884">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/545636884</a>
Measurement Measure through Web Platform Test results, Interop 2026 WebTransport results, and developer feedback. No dedicated UMA metric is planned because this is an additive capability-reporting API that does not change network behavior.
Availability expectation Expected to become available across major browser engines as part of the W3C WebTransport specification. WebKit implements both attributes, while Firefox currently implements the per-session reliability attribute
Adoption expectation Expected to be adopted by WebTransport applications that use datagrams or need to operate across transports with different reliability capabilities.
Adoption plan Adoption is expected to happen organically as WebTransport applications use these attributes to select between reliable streams and unreliable datagrams.
Non-OSS dependencies
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function? No
Estimated milestones
Shipping on desktop 158
DevTrial on desktop 155
Shipping on Android 158
DevTrial on Android 155
Shipping on WebView 158
Anticipated spec changes
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). None. The attributes and WebTransportReliabilityMode values are already defined in the W3C WebTransport specification.
