<pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2
/Daniel</pre><pre>
On 2026-10-21 17:31, Yoav Weiss (@Shopify) wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM1
On Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 11:08:15 PM UTC+2 Chromestatus wrote:
*Contact emails* <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="374155454e5f5e191919775a5e544558445851431954585a">[email protected]</a>
*Explainer* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/544">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/544</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/544">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/544</a>> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/574">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/574</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/574">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/574</a>>
*Specification* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-configuration">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-configuration</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-configuration">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-configuration</a>>
*Summary* Allows WebTransport applications to indicate how many incoming streams they expect to have open at once. Constructor hints configure the initial QUIC stream allowance, reducing the risk that a server that needs high stream concurrency is blocked by the initial stream limit.
*Blink component* Blink>Network>WebTransport
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>>
*Web Feature ID* webtransport <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>>
*Motivation* Some WebTransport applications expect a server to open many streams at once. If the initial QUIC stream allowance is too low, the server must wait for more stream credit before opening additional streams, adding avoidable latency or limiting the number of open streams. Constructor hints let the application state its expected stream count when creating the connection, so the browser can advertise an appropriate initial allowance. Values above the required minimum are preserved; values below 100 do not reduce the effective allowance because the specification requires clients to initially permit at least 100 streams of each type.
*Initial public proposal* /No information provided/
*TAG review* This is a small incremental addition to an existing feature which is already standardized.
*TAG review status* Not applicable
*Goals for experimentation* None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility* Compatibility risk is low because this is an additive API. Existing sites that do not use the new names are unaffected. Interoperability risk is low to moderate: WebKit implements these specific members, while Firefox supports WebTransport but does not currently expose them.
/Gecko/: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007825">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007825</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007825">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2007825</a>>) Firefox supports WebTransport, but not these two anticipated-incoming-stream members. Implementation work is in progress, no shipping milestone is announced.
/WebKit/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://commits.webkit.org/303419@main">https://commits.webkit.org/303419@main</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://commits.webkit.org/303419@main">https://commits.webkit.org/303419@main</a>>) Implemented in WebKit revision 303419@main and shipped in Safari 26.4, including Safari on iOS.
/Web developers/: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 positive reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
/Other signals/:
*Ergonomics* The constructor options are nullable unsigned-short hints and default to null. The corresponding attributes expose the currently stored values. [EnforceRange] rejects values outside the unsigned-short range. Values below 100 remain visible through the attributes but cannot reduce the effective initial stream allowance below the specification-required minimum.
*Activation* No permission or user activation is required beyond the existing WebTransport requirements. A site opts in by supplying either constructor option.
*Security* This does not grant a new capability or expose application data. It lets a site request a bounded initial stream allowance for its existing secure-context WebTransport connection. Stream credit does not eagerly allocate all streams.
*WebView application risks*
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications?
Low. The change is additive and does not modify behavior for applications that do not use the new options or attributes. The implementation uses the existing cross-platform WebTransport connection stack.
*Debuggability* The hints can be inspected through the JavaScript attributes. Existing DevTools and NetLog support for WebTransport and QUIC remains applicable.
*Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)?* Yes
*Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>?* Yes
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/anticipated-concurrent-incoming-streams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/anticipated-concurrent-incoming-streams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/anticipated-concurrent-incoming-streams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/anticipated-concurrent-incoming-streams.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master</a>>
*Flag name on about://flags* enable-experimental-web-platform-features
*Finch feature name* WebTransportAnticipatedConcurrentIncomingStreams
*Rollout plan* Will ship enabled for all users
*Requires code in //chrome?* False
*Tracking bug* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/565837025">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/565837025</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/565837025">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/565837025</a>>
*Availability expectation* The API is part of the W3C WebTransport specification and is implemented by WebKit/Safari. Firefox supports WebTransport but does not yet expose these specific members. Cross-browser availability is expected to improve as implementations converge on the current WebTransport specification.
*Adoption expectation* Adoption is expected among WebTransport applications whose servers need to create more than the minimum number of streams concurrently, including real-time communication, media, gaming, remote interaction, and multiplexed application protocols. Broader adoption will follow overall WebTransport usage.
*Adoption plan* No dedicated outreach campaign is planned. Adoption is expected through WebTransport documentation, examples, and client/server library support.
*Non-OSS dependencies*
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function?
No.
*Estimated milestones* Shipping on desktop 158 DevTrial on desktop 151 Shipping on Android 158 DevTrial on Android 151 Shipping on WebView 158
*Anticipated spec changes*
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (e.g. links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (e.g., changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way).
None known for these constructor options or attributes. The wider WebTransport specification continues to progress, but no known open issue requires a breaking change to these members before launch.

entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Prototype%5C%3A+document.advanceFocus%5C%28%5C%29+and+beforefocus%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Prototype: document.advanceFocus() and beforefocus</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22%27Marat+Abdullin%27+via+blink%5C-dev%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">'Marat Abdullin' via blink-dev</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261021" rel="nofollow">Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:38:21 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails
Marat Abdullin <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="92fff3e0bcbcbcd2fffbf1e0fde1fdf4e6bcf1fdff">[email protected]</a><<a rel="nofollow" href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#345955461a1a1a74595d57465b475b52401a575b59">mailto:<span class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="fc919d8ed2d2d2bc91959f8e938f939a88d29f9391">[email protected]</span></a>></pre><pre>
Explainer
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://open-ui.org/components/beforefocus.explainer">https://open-ui.org/components/beforefocus.explainer</a>
Specification
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://open-ui.org/components/beforefocus.explainer">https://open-ui.org/components/beforefocus.explainer</a>
This is an incubating design, not yet an adopted standard. Proposed HTML integration: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13104">https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13104</a>.
Summary
document.advanceFocus() lets a page move focus using the browser's own Tab order, with options for direction, starting point, containment and wrapping. It returns a Promise reporting the outcome. The cancelable beforefocus event lets a page stop a focus move before an element receives focus.
Blink component
Blink>HTML>Focus
Web Feature ID
Not assigned; requested in: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4558">https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4558</a>.
Motivation
Dialogs, keyboard navigation and protection against focus theft often require apps to reconstruct focus order or redirect focus after it has moved. These primitives let apps use the browser's navigation instead, including across shadow DOM and embedded frames.
Initial public proposal
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1261">https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1261</a>
Goals for experimentation
No origin trial is proposed. The current work is limited to off-by-default prototyping and feedback on API ergonomics and safe focus interception.
Requires code in //chrome?
No. The current Chromium prototype does not change files under //chrome.
Tracking bug
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/575489395">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/575489395</a>
Measurement
The Blink WIP prototype adds DocumentAdvanceFocus for method calls and BeforeFocusEvent for browser-generated event dispatch. Implementation: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8612302">https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8612302</a>. These are prototype use counters, not an assigned Web Feature ID.
Estimated milestones
None proposed; this is an off-by-default prototype, not a shipping request.
Link to entry on the Chrome Platform Status
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5134711960764416?gate=5156755611975680">https://chromestatus.com/feature/5134711960764416?gate=5156755611975680</a>
Prototype and related work
Chromium implementation: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/8612302">https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/8612302</a>.
In a build containing the Chromium patch, enable FocusNavigation with --enable-blink-features=FocusNavigation; pages also opt in with:
<meta name="focus-navigation" content="advanceFocus beforefocus">
The Chromium and Firefox prototypes have matching tentative WPTs, supplemented by native tests.
Blink test review: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8612302/2">https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8612302/2</a>.
Gecko test review: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D335668?id=1414112">https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D335668?id=1414112</a>.
These are browser-prototype review links, not a standalone upstream WPT PR. A single upstream export remains to be coordinated.
Firefox tracking: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2084212">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2084212</a>. Firefox intent: planned. I will reply here with the dev-platform thread once it is public. Firefox implementation: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D335668">https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D335668</a>.
I welcome feedback on API ergonomics and safe focus interception, particularly keyboard and assistive-technology behavior. These are contributor-maintained prototypes, not independent vendor endorsements. Current local testing is on macOS, not all platforms.
This intent message uses the Chrome Platform Status generated template, supplemented with prototype details.
Thanks, Marat Abdullin

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Re%5C%3A+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+receive+stream%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Ship: WebTransport receive stream</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Mike+Taylor%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Mike Taylor</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261028" rel="nofollow">Wed, 28 Oct 2026 19:46:04 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM3
On 10/28/26 5:20 a.m., Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2</pre><pre></pre><tt>On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 7:03 PM Alex Russell </tt><tt><<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="71021d181619051d085f5f5f311219031e1c18041c5f1e0316">[email protected]</a>> wrote: </tt><pre style="margin: 0em;">
LGTM1; love to see these practical additions!
On Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 6:31:37 PM UTC-7 Chromestatus wrote:
*Contact emails* <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="4c3a2e3e3524256262620c21252f3e233f232a38622f2321">[email protected]</a>
*Explainer* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/372">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/372</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/395">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/395</a>
*Specification* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#webtransportreceivestream">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#webtransportreceivestream</a>
*Summary* Adds the standardized WebTransportReceiveStream interface, a ReadableStream subclass used for incoming unidirectional streams and the readable side of bidirectional streams. Its getStats() method returns per-stream byte counters: bytesReceived reports bytes received from the network, while bytesRead reports bytes delivered to the application.
*Blink component* Blink>Network>WebTransport
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>>
*Web Feature ID* webtransport <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>>
*Motivation* Incoming WebTransport streams have historically been exposed as generic ReadableStream objects in Chromium. The WebTransport specification defines a dedicated WebTransportReceiveStream subclass with stream-specific statistics. Applications that receive large or latency-sensitive streams need to distinguish bytes received by the browser from bytes actually consumed by JavaScript. This helps diagnose application backpressure, buffering, and slow-consumer behavior. Exposing the standardized subclass also aligns the runtime type of incoming streams with the WebTransport specification and other browser engines.
*Initial public proposal* /No information provided/
*TAG review* /No information provided/
*TAG review status* Not applicable
*Goals for experimentation* None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility* Enabling this feature changes incoming unidirectional streams and the readable side of bidirectional streams from plain ReadableStream objects to WebTransportReceiveStream objects. Reading remains compatible, and the objects remain instanceof ReadableStream, but applications that compare the exact constructor or prototype may observe a change. Firefox and Safari already expose WebTransportReceiveStream, so this aligns Chrome’s stream type with those browsers.
/Gecko/: Under consideration (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webidl/WebTransportSendReceiveStream.webidl">https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webidl/WebTransportSendReceiveStream.webidl</a>) Partial implementation. Firefox ships WebTransportReceiveStream and exposes getStats(), but getStats() currently rejects with NotSupportedError, so receive stream statistics are not implemented. Implementation

The interface is not constructible directly; applications obtain it from incomingUnidirectionalStreams or from the readable side of a bidirectional stream. Chromium's IDL currently types WebTransportBidirectionalStream.readable as ReadableStream because Blink cannot conditionally change an IDL attribute type behind a runtime flag, although the returned object is a WebTransportReceiveStream when the feature is enabled.
*Activation* Activation is automatic for sites using incoming WebTransport streams; no server change or opt-in is required. Existing code that treats these objects as ReadableStream continues to work because WebTransportReceiveStream is a subclass.
